- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.20) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture sharp downside reversals.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays reaction to sentiment shifts, especially after strong negative sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to premature retracement in true price paths.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days of forecast horizon) — especially when sentiment turns bullish.
- Avoid averaging sentiment across all days — weight recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) more heavily for short-term price adjustments.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: model often overreacts to sentiment turning negative, leading to exaggerated downward corrections.
